$schema: Defines the complete Figma variable collection architecture — all collections, their variable types, naming conventions, scoping rules, mode configuration, and code syntax format. Components consume these variables directly during generation; no component-level variable collections.

primitives.color.description: Raw color palette values. All hex → 0-1 float conversion at generation time.

primitives.spacing.description: Universal spacing scale. Single source for all gap, padding, and dimensional values.

primitives.radius.description: Border radius primitives. Full scale from sharp to pill.

primitives.component-height.description: Component height scale. Used for buttons, inputs, list items, nav bars, etc.

primitives.typography.description: Typography property variables. Text styles bind to these — changing a variable cascades through all bound text styles.

primitives.effects.description: Shadow property primitives. Effect styles bind individual properties (offset-y, blur, spread) to these variables. Shadow color stays in the effect style directly (Figma limitation).

semantic.color.description: Semantic color roles. Aliases primitive colors. Light and dark modes swap which primitives are referenced.
semantic.color.alias-pattern: Each variable aliases a primitives.color variable. Mode determines which primitive: light.primary → primitives.color/primary/600, dark.primary → primitives.color/primary/400.

semantic.spacing.description: Categorical spacing values. Default and compact variants as separate paths, not modes. Aliases primitive spacing scale.
semantic.spacing.variant-note: Default and compact are separate variable paths, not Figma modes. A designer picks spacing/section/default/x-padding or spacing/section/compact/x-padding explicitly. Compact is a per-context choice, not a global swap.

semantic.radius.description: Semantic border-radius roles. Aliases primitive radius values.

semantic.component-height.description: Control height roles. Aliases primitives.component-height. This layer is what a project's controlHeight answer (compact / standard / touch) actually selects — the same role names resolve to different ch-* steps per ladder. Without it the pasted file states heights as raw primitives, so two projects with opposite ladders produce identical height variables and a designer cannot see that button/md and text-field/md are one decision.
semantic.component-height.primitive-note: Avatar portraits and stepper indicators deliberately stay on primitives.component-height — they are sized objects, not controls, so they take no role.

semantic.opacity.description: State opacity roles. The one semantic collection that resolves to literal values rather than aliasing a primitive layer — opacity has no underlying scale, so disabled and muted are the whole set. Naming them primitives would have taught the next reader that the layer names do not mean anything.

figma.layout.description: Documentation-specific layout values. Hue-neutral, mode-independent. COLOR values are direct hex (not semantic aliases). FLOAT spacing values alias primitives.spacing. Includes surface elevations and outline levels.

text-styles.description: Figma text styles bound to primitives.typography variables. One style per typography preset. Changing a typography variable cascades through all bound text styles.
examples: display → binds to type/display/size, type/display/height, type/family/body, type/display/weight
body → binds to type/body/size, type/body/height, type/family/body, type/body/weight
caption → binds to type/caption/size, type/caption/height, type/family/body, type/caption/weight

effect-styles.description: Figma effect styles for shadows. Individual properties (offset-y, blur, spread) bind to primitives.effects variables. Shadow color is set directly (not variable-bindable — Figma limitation).
effect-styles.binding-method: Set boundVariables on effect object, then reassign effects array. setBoundVariable() does NOT work on effect styles.
examples: shadow/1 → binds offsetY, radius, spread to shadow/1/* primitives

component-generation.description: Components do NOT have their own variable collections. During generation, the script reads component configs and binds Figma component properties directly to semantic/primitive variables. This keeps the variable panel clean and human-navigable.
component-generation.approach: The generation script reads config/components/*.json, builds Figma components, and binds fills/spacing/typography to existing semantic and primitive variables. No intermediate variable layer.
component-generation.override-strategy: If a project needs component-level variable overrides (e.g., all buttons use a non-standard radius), add a targeted collection at that time — not preemptively.
binding-examples: Button filled/primary bg → binds to semantic.color/primary/primary
Button sm x-padding → binds to primitives.spacing/3
Card default radius → binds to semantic.radius/card
Toast shadow → applies effect style shadow/3

scoping-rules.description: Each variable type is scoped to restrict where it appears in the Figma variable picker. This prevents misuse (e.g., picking a spacing value for a color fill).

code-syntax-format.description: All variables get WEB code syntax set via setVariableCodeSyntax('WEB', ...). This appears in Figma Dev Mode when inspecting elements.
code-syntax-format.note: Figma also supports ANDROID and iOS platforms — deferred until needed.
